identity.name: Oirat Confederation (17th century)
alt_names: Oirat union of the Dzungar basin

land.text: the Oirat lands of western Mongolia and the Altai that the Eastern Mongols 'pushed ... westward' from 1480

predecessors.note: four-oirats now runs to 1608 and meets this dossier's found of 1609 with no gap (fix batch fx-51, 2 Nov 2026). Earlier note: The four-oirats dossier (1399-1480) names this state as its successor line. The Oirat page: 'From 1480 on, the Eastern Mongols under Mandukhai Khatun and Dayan Khan pushed the Oirats westward'; by 1510 Dayan Khan 'had unified the Mongol tribes, including the Oirats'. Cliopatria has no Oirat row for 1475-1608, so 129 years separate the two dossiers.

land.text: the Dzungarian core on the upper Emil River and the Junggar basin, 365,737 km2

successors.note: Dzungar page infobox 'Established: 1634' with '1634: Oirat confederation' as predecessor; the Oirat page: 'Disestablished: 1634', successors the Dzungar, Kalmyk and Khoshut khanates. The Dzungar dossier draws the Oirat rows of 1634-1676 as its own keyframes.

land.text: Qinghai (Koke Nuur) and then Tibet, where 'Gushi Khan went ... in 1636' with 10,000 Oirats

successors.note: The Khoshut khanate is named as a successor in the Oirat page's infobox; its land is outside Cliopatria's Oirat shape.

land.text: the lower Volga where the Torghut and Dorbets settled in 1630

successors.note: The Torghut and some Dorbets left the upper Irtysh in 1618 (Kalmyks page) or 1628 (Oirat page); the Kalmyk page: 'Upon arrival in the lower Volga region in 1630'.

correction.text: the Dzungarian core of the Oirats, 365,737 km2 (Cliopatria's Dzungar row of 1609-1618)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1609-1618: Cliopatria draws this land (365,737 km2, 79.9-91.0 E, 42.2-49.6 N: Dzungaria) as 'Dzungar Khanate' for 1609-1618 and as 'Oirat Confederation' from 1619, with the identical area. The Dzungar page has the Oirats active here before the khanate: 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz, subjugating them in the process' and 'About 1620 the western Mongols, known as the Oirats, united in the Junggar Basin in Dzungaria'. The Dzungar Khanate itself is 'Established: 1634', so the shape is drawn here.

correction.text: unchanged shape, years 1619-1634; from 1634 it is drawn by dzungar-khanate

keyframe_review.note: 365,737 km2 for 1619-1635 (79.9-91.0 E, 42.2-49.6 N): the Junggar basin and the Tian Shan slopes round Ghulja, where the Oirats united about 1620. Right for 1619-1634; the Oirat page has 'Disestablished: 1634' and the Dzungar Khanate takes the same outline from 1634, so 1635 belongs to the Dzungar dossier. The Oirat page gives no area figure.

correction.text: use the 365,737 km2 core for 1636-1657, drawn by dzungar-khanate; the 839,091 km2 outline only from 1658

keyframe_review.note: 839,091 km2 for 1636-1658 (73.4-91.0 E, 38.5-49.6 N): no page opened puts an Oirat state of this size in these years. The Oirat Confederation was disestablished in 1634 and the Dzungar Khanate founded; the pages show raids and fighting for Semirechye (1635 Jangir captured, winter 1643, 1645-46, 1652) and the border fixed 'from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River' only after the victory of 1658. The 365,737 km2 core is used for 1636-1657 (dzungar-khanate_1634) and this outline from 1658 (dzungar-khanate_1658). Infobox area (Dzungar page, '1650: 3,600,000 km2') is 4.3 times this shape; it matches the Dzungar peak under Galdan (1687-1695), so the infobox year is probably wrong.

correction.text: unchanged shape, reassigned to dzungar-khanate (keyframe dzungar-khanate_1658)

keyframe_review.note: 838,700 km2 for 1659-1669, the 1658 outline (the Chu and Talas victory, the Ayagoz-Talas border). The state is the Dzungar Khanate (established 1634); this dossier ended in 1634.

838,755 km2 for 1670-1672, the same outline; Sengge is assassinated in 1670 (Chechen Tayiji and Zotov's coup) and Galdan wins in 1671 ('In 1671, The Dalai Lama bestowed the title of Khan on Galdan'); the state is the Dzungar Khanate, not an Oirat confederation, in these years.

838,755 km2 for 1673-1676, the same outline; 'In 1676, Galdan defeated Chechen near Sayram Lake' and the victory over Ochirtu in 1677 gave him 'domination of the Oirats' - the Dzungar Khanate again, as Cliopatria's own Dzungar row resumes in 1677.

region.text: the Junggar basin and the Tian Shan slopes, 365,737 km2

ledger.note: 1609: the Oirat realm of Dzungaria enters the map. Cliopatria's first row for the land is 1609; the Dzungar page: 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz, subjugating them in the process' and 'About 1620 the western Mongols, known as the Oirats, united in the Junggar Basin in Dzungaria' (Cliopatria's Oirat row begins 1619). The year 1609 is Cliopatria's; no page names a founding.

region.text: the lower Volga north of the Caspian, where the Torghut and Dorbets founded the Kalmyk Khanate

ledger.note: 1628: the Torghut and Dorbets leave for the Volga. 'The collapse of the confederation of the Oirats began with Torghuds': Khoo Orlug led Torghuts, Dorbets and some Khoshuts westward across the Kazakh steppes in 1628 (infobox: 'Movement of the Torghuds to the Volga: 1616-17'; Kalmyks page: left the upper Irtysh in 1618, arrived 1630). The land they left is on no page; the region is where they settled. Confidence 2 (reviewer ia-03-d, 2026-10-19): the page dates the move (1628) but names no land beyond 'westward across the Kazakh steppes'; the Volga region is the researcher's reading.

1634: the Oirat Confederation gives way to the Dzungar Khanate. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1634' with the successors 'Dzungar Khanate, Kalmyk Khanate, Khoshut Khanate' and 'Establishment of the Dzungar and Khoshut Khanates: 1630s'; the Dzungar page 'Established: 1634'. The Dzungar dossier founds in the same year on the same cells.

wars.name: Oirat-Khalkha wars
wars.outcome: No frontier moved: the Khalkha 'repeatedly launched massive attacks on the Oirats' (1552-1628), looting the Irtysh, Barkol and Altai; the Oirats crushed the Khalkha prince Sholoi Ubashi 'perhaps around 1623'; peace with the Khalkha came after Ligdan Khan died in 1634.
wars.note: The Dzungar page: 'The Oirats had established peace with the Khalkha Mongols since Ligdan Khan died in 1634'.

wars.name: Oirat campaigns against the Kazakhs and Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz, subjugating them in the process'; no land is named and no border moved.

certainty.note: Pastoral frontiers in the Junggar basin and the Tian Shan; no page describes a boundary.

notes:
Cliopatria row reviewed: Oirat Confederation (1619-1676, 5 shapes). SAME STATE AS FOUR OIRATS? NO. Cliopatria's Oirat Confederation shares Wikidata Q4332415 with 'Four Oirats' (the 15th-century realm of the Choros taishis, 1399-1480, dossier four-oirats by the earlier run). They are two polities 129 years apart (1480 to 1609), so Cliopatria's Oirat Confederation is not a continuation of the Four Oirats row; this dossier names four-oirats as predecessor. The Wikipedia article 'Oirat Confederation' treats one confederation from 1399 to 1634.

THE RELATION TO THE DZUNGAR KHANATE (decision to review). Cliopatria draws one continuous realm under three labels: 'Dzungar Khanate' 1609-1618, 'Oirat Confederation' 1619-1676 (shapes of identical area: 365,737 km2, then 839,091 km2 from 1636) and 'Dzungar Khanate' again from 1677. The pages disagree with the 1676 break: the Dzungar page gives 'Established: 1634' and the Oirat page 'Disestablished: 1634'. This dossier therefore runs 1609-1634 (start moved back from Cliopatria's 1619 to 1609, because the Dzungar row has the same shape from 1609 and the Dzungar page has Oirat activity in 1609-1616; the 1609 start is a confidence-1 event) and marks the Oirat rows of 1636-1676 wrong for its own years; dzungar-khanate carries them as new keyframes from 1634. The handoff year 1634 is drawn by both dossiers on identical cells.
CONSEQUENCE FOR OTHER DOSSIERS: kazakh-khanate's ledger (1643 contest_start, 1658 contest_end and loss) names oirat-confederation as counterpart; with this split it should read dzungar-khanate. If a reviewer prefers Cliopatria's partition (Oirat to 1676, Dzungar from 1677), the two dossiers can be swapped back by moving the new keyframes; the alternative of one dossier for the whole realm (cliopatria_names both) is also available.

Silent pages: the Oirat Confederation page has no word on Khara Khula, Erdeni Batur, the 1620s union (apart from 'perhaps around 1623' for the defeat of Sholoi Ubashi), the Ochirtu-Galdan war or any area; the founding year of the Dzungar state is the Dzungar page's. The Torghut departure is dated 1628 (text), 1616-17 (infobox) and 1618 (Kalmyks page). The land the Torghuts left is not named. The Khoshut move to Qinghai 'in 1636' is after this dossier's end and belongs to khoshut-khanate. Capital: the infobox gives 'Not given', so none. Rulers: the page lists none after 1469.

Pages: five opened (Oirat Confederation, Dzungar Khanate, Kazakh-Dzungar Wars, Kalmyk Khanate, Kalmyks), four of them shared with the dzungar-khanate and kalmyk-khanate dossiers.
